items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: I have a friend, Noah Brandmark that played with Woody Herman

ctx.x: Did you actually play with your upper lip under your teeth?

Well he had, put your head down a little bit, you know he taught Stan Getz and all his students. But I don’t think you need this other than support and with the slightest support, just be centered in the middle of the mouthpiece. But I have a friend, Noah Brandmark that played with Woody Herman, that had a great sound. And it took me until I was about 30 to have a sound like him, and he was 14 when we met. He was only studying a half year with Bill Shiner and he had this mature sound. I wasn’t jealous we were…

through it you don’t need your lip. I’m being silly. Or cardboard. And make it vibrate. I was just clamping on the opening of the reed. So I have them start from nothing and blow, and blow as full as you can, but when your lip is on the reed if you’re not putting any pressure at all it’s not going to vibrate yet. So I said slowly get tighter and eventually clamp the reed. And back off slowly until you are vibrating. And you’re getting like, I call it a buzz like in your oral cavity. I can’t explain it. But it’s…
